current_example.problem:
Find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow -2}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{x^2-1}\right)^{2/3}$ for the function $f(x)$ plotted below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14198442/assets/583e67513466b35aafcae69c81d5703b45ffada4bdc08bb34de15ee6ce1d53e5.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
According to the power rule and the quotient rules,

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -2}{(\frac{f(x)}{{x}^{2}-1})}^{2/3} & ={(\frac{{lim}_{x\to -2}f(x)}{{lim}_{x\to -2}({x}^{2}-1)})}^{2/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We find from the graph that the limit of the numerator is

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow -2} f(x)=1.
$$

 We also calculate the limit of the denominator as
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -2}({x}^{2}-1) & =(-2)^{2}-1=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 So we get
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -2}{(\frac{f(x)}{{x}^{2}-1})}^{2/3} & ={(\frac{{lim}_{x\to -2}f(x)}{{lim}_{x\to -2}({x}^{2}-1)})}^{2/3} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{2/3} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{9}}.\end{aligned}
$$
